reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its observable purpose is to explain several online-income approaches while warning viewers about scams in some work-from-home contexts and possible cheating during OLX transactions. The earning website, referral figures, account information, and displayed brokerage referral page are described as discussion or promotion of methods and terms, without evidence of deception, theft, completed loss, or a confirmed outcome. the available video evidence does not establish that the presenter endorsed every displayed service, so these details remain contextual rather than sufficient evidence of a scam mechanism.

opening.argument: Judge the stock-referral pitch as a promise tied to an action, not merely a discussion of earning options. Viewers are directed to links in the description to earn money, and the speaker says one referral pays 400 rupees and ten in a month bring about 4000 rupees, calling that amount guaranteed. The description supplies stock-market earning links. That sequence invites viewers to use the links and recruit others on the strength of a stated payout.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The YouTube, affiliate-marketing and OLX examples show that the video covers several methods; they do not neutralize the separate referral solicitation. The defense itself identifies the instruction to use description links. The disputed point is the certainty attached to that action: the speaker calls the projected referral earnings guaranteed.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The links and payout estimate establish promotion of a referral method, but not a deceptive payout or a loss. The speaker also says trading can carry annual maintenance charges, qualifying the broader no-payment pitch. Nothing cited shows that the stated referral amount was unavailable or that a viewer was misled into paying.

opening.argument: The risk signal is the combination of easy-income language and a request for financial contact details. The speaker says visiting a named website can earn viewers a lot of money, then says they may send an email address or bank account number. In the stock-referral discussion, he says identity and bank details are needed and describes a monthly referral amount as guaranteed. These are more consequential claims than a general suggestion to try online work: they put promised income beside requests for sensitive information.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Warnings about data-entry scams and cheating on OLX do not answer the concern about this different earning pitch. Nor does the absence of a documented loss resolve what viewers are being encouraged to do. The speaker links a prospect of substantial earnings to visiting a website and potentially providing an email address or bank account number; that invitation deserves scrutiny on its own terms.

The video also discusses documents and bank proof in connection with receiving affiliate earnings. Treating mention of those details as evidence of a deceptive collection scheme goes beyond what is shown.

opening.argument: The educational format also serves a promotional purpose. After discussing YouTube and affiliate marketing, the speaker calls the stock-market route a genuine way to earn, tells viewers to use links in the description, and presents referral income as guaranteed at the stated monthly example. The description contains a joining link and stock-market earning links. Those calls to participate make the video more than an overview of possible work: it steers viewers from advice toward a specific earning route.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the referral material as discussion or promotion, but promotion is precisely why the broader tutorial framing cannot settle the question. The speaker does not merely name a method; he directs viewers to description links to earn money. His separate YouTube and OLX advice does not erase that invitation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A promotional call to use referral links is not, by itself, evidence that the offer is deceptive. The speaker presents it among several methods, including building a YouTube channel and reselling products, and notes that trading can entail annual maintenance charges. The prosecution identifies participation and an optimistic earnings claim, but no false term, concealed payment or demonstrated loss.
